title: Why Does My Dryer Take Two Cycles to Dry?
h1: Why Does My Dryer Take Two Cycles to Dry Clothes?
description: A dryer that needs two cycles usually has a clogged or crushed vent. Learn the quick checks, the other likely causes and when to call for vent cleaning.
quick_answer: The most common reason a dryer needs two cycles is a restricted vent. Lint buildup, a crushed or kinked hose, a long vent run or a stuck outside flap traps hot, wet air in the drum. Overloading, a dirty lint screen or a failing moisture sensor can also cause it. Check the vent first, because a clogged vent is also a fire risk.
body:
When a dryer suddenly needs two cycles, the vent is the first place to look. A dryer works by pushing hot, moist air out of the house. If lint, a kink or a stuck flap slows that airflow, the moisture has nowhere to go, and clothes stay damp no matter how hot the drum gets.

A blocked vent isn't just slow. Lint is very flammable, and a dryer that runs hot for long periods with poor airflow is a real fire hazard.

What quick checks can I do myself?

Start with these simple checks before calling anyone:

  1. Clean the lint screen. Do it every load. If it looks clean but water beads on it, wash it with warm soapy water, since dryer sheet residue can clog the mesh.
  2. Look at the hose behind the dryer. Pull the dryer out a few inches and check for a crushed, kinked or disconnected transition hose.
  3. Check the outside vent. Run the dryer and go outside. You should feel strong, warm airflow, and the flap should open fully.
  4. Look at the vent hood. Lint, bird nests and paint can jam the flap or screen, which traps air.
  5. Feel the dryer. If the top or sides are much hotter than usual, airflow is probably restricted.

If airflow outside is weak, the restriction is somewhere in the vent run, and that's where cleaning comes in.

Why do dryer vents clog?

Lint screens catch most lint, but not all of it. The rest travels into the vent and sticks to the walls, especially at elbows and low spots. Over time, it narrows the duct. Some setups clog faster than others:

  • Long vent runs with several turns
  • Vents that exit through the roof, which is common in condos and some two-story homes
  • Foil or vinyl flex hose with ridges that trap lint
  • Vents that sag in the attic or under the floor, where moisture and lint collect
  • Busy households doing laundry every day

What else can make a dryer take two cycles?

If the vent is clear, these are the next suspects:

  • Overloading. Clothes need room to tumble. A packed drum dries slowly.
  • Washer not spinning well. If clothes come out of the washer soaking wet, the dryer has more work to do.
  • Wrong setting. Low heat or a delicate cycle on heavy towels will take longer.
  • Moisture sensor problems. Sensor bars inside the drum can get coated with fabric softener residue and shut the cycle off early. Wiping them with rubbing alcohol often helps.
  • Heating problems. A failed heating element on an electric dryer or an igniter problem on a gas dryer means little or no heat.

Leave heating element, gas valve and wiring repairs to an appliance technician. If you ever smell gas near a gas dryer, leave the house and call the gas utility from outside.

When should I call for dryer vent cleaning?

Call if the quick checks don't fix it, if airflow outside is weak, if you see lint around the outside hood, or if you notice a burning smell when the dryer runs. Also call if your vent is long, runs through the roof or hasn't been cleaned in a year or more.

Our dryer vent cleaning service clears the full run from the dryer to the outside, checks the hood and flap, and replaces crushed or plastic transition hose with a safer metal connector. If the run is too long or has too many turns, we can talk about rerouting it.

How can I keep it from happening again?

Clean the lint screen every load, keep the dryer from being pushed tight against the wall, and check the outside flap every few months. Use rigid or semi-rigid metal duct, not plastic or foil. And schedule vent cleaning about once a year, or more often for long runs and busy laundry rooms. You can check our specials for current dryer vent offers.
faqs: Is it dangerous if my dryer takes two cycles?

It can be. Slow drying often means restricted airflow, which makes the dryer run hotter and longer with lint in the vent. That's a fire risk. Get the vent checked and cleaned rather than just running extra cycles.
How do I know if my dryer vent is clogged?
Common signs include clothes taking longer to dry, weak airflow at the outside vent, a hot dryer cabinet, lint around the outside hood and a burning smell. Any of these is worth checking.
Can a long dryer vent cause slow drying?
Yes. Every foot of duct and every elbow adds resistance. Dryer manufacturers list a maximum vent length, and runs near or over that limit dry slower and clog faster. Rerouting may help.
Is a foil dryer hose safe?
Foil and plastic hoses crush easily and their ridges trap lint. Rigid or semi-rigid metal duct is the safer choice for the connection behind the dryer and for the rest of the run.
